newsitem.title: USA: Moody's ups PETRO Trust asset-backed notes.
newsitem.headline: Moody's ups PETRO Trust asset-backed notes.

text.p: NEW YORK, May 16 - Moody's Investors Service has raised its rating to Baa2 from Baa3 on approximately $220 million of Floating Rate Asset-Backed Notes due February 5, 2003, issued by Petroleum Enhanced Trust Receivables Offering (PETRO) Trust.
Moody's rating change primarily reflects our December 1996 upgrade of the senior unsecured debt of Occidental Petroleum Corporation (OPC) to Baa2.
OPC guarantees the punctual payment and performance of Occidental C.O.B. Partners to deliver crude oil to the trust and of Occidental Crude Sales, Inc. to purchase crude oil from the trust.

The rating of the PETRO Trust Notes also reflects: a Goldman Sachs Group, L.P. (Goldman Sachs) guarantee of the prompt and complete payment by J. Aron & Company under an oil swap and interest rate swap; a liquidity facility furnished by Goldman Sachs; a letter of credit issued by Bank of America National Trust and Savings Association (Bank of America); and the satisfactory historical performance of the trust since its formation in November 1996.

These securities were sold in a privately negotiated transaction without registration under the Securities Act of 1933 (the Act) under circumstances reasonably designed to preclude a distribution thereof in violation of the Act.
The issuance has been designed to permit resale under Rule 144A. Moody's rates the senior unsecured debt of Goldman Sachs A1 and the senior unsecured bank note program of Bank of America Aa3.
